title: combine increasing/decreasing with concavity on a quarter-period of a sine or cosine graph, including a reflected curve.
stem: On the interval 0 < x < 2π, which open interval of the graph of y = sin x is both increasing and concave down?

choices.label: A
choices.rationale: Correct: For y = sin x the slope sign and second-derivative sign by quadrant give increasing and concave down only on (0, π/2).

choices.label: B
choices.rationale: On (π/2, π) the graph is concave down there but it is decreasing, so only one of the two conditions holds.

choices.label: C
choices.rationale: On (π, 3π/2) the graph is decreasing and concave up there, which meets neither condition.

choices.label: D
choices.rationale: On (3π/2, 2π) the graph is increasing there but it is concave up, so only one of the two conditions holds.

choices.rationale: Correct: Amplitude = (11 − 3)/2 = 4; midline y = 7; half period 6 so period 12 and b = π/6; a maximum at x = 2 gives cosine shifted 2.

choices.label: B
choices.rationale: This uses the distance between the two points as the full period, but it is only half a period, so the argument should be π(x − h)/6 and the graph repeats too quickly.

choices.label: C

stem: The graph of y = sin x is stretched vertically by a factor of 3, compressed horizontally so that its period is π, and then translated right π/4 and up 2. Which equation describes the new graph?

choices.label: A
choices.rationale: Correct: Amplitude 3, b = 2π/π = 2, right shift π/4 gives sin(2(x − π/4)), up 2.

choices.label: B
choices.rationale: This subtracts π/4 after multiplying by 2, which shifts the graph right only π/8, not π/4.

choices.label: C
choices.rationale: This has a plus sign inside the parentheses, which shifts the graph left π/4 instead of right.

choices.label: D
choices.rationale: This divides x by 2, which stretches the period to 4π, but a period of π needs b = 2π/π = 2.

choices.label: B
choices.rationale: This divides only the π by b and subtracts c unscaled, but the shift c must also be divided by b.

choices.label: C

choices.label: D
choices.rationale: Correct: Maximum (4) needs cos(2x + π/3) = −1, so 2x + π/3 = π + 2πk, giving x = π/3 for the least positive value (f there = 4).

title: choose the cosine model that fits a described context (starting position or time of an extreme, range, period), with sig
stem: A Ferris wheel has diameter 40 meters and its center is 22 meters above the ground. It makes one full rotation every 30 seconds. A rider boards at the lowest point of the wheel at time t = 0 seconds. Which function gives the rider's height h(t), in meters above the ground, at time t seconds?

stem: The function g is defined by g(x) = −3tan(x − π/4) + 1. The graph of g has a vertical asymptote at x = 3π/4. What happens to g(x) as x approaches 3π/4 from the left?

choices.label: A
choices.rationale: This has the direction reversed: near this asymptote the tangent part goes to +∞, and the factor −3 flips that direction, so g goes to −∞.

choices.label: B
choices.rationale: This treats the vertical shift as a horizontal asymptote, but a tangent graph has no horizontal asymptote; its values are unbounded near a vertical asymptote.

choices.label: C
choices.rationale: Correct: Approaching from the left, the inside expression approaches an odd multiple of π/2 from below, so the tangent part goes to +∞; multiplying by −3 gives −∞. Numerical check: g at 1e−7 left of the asymptote is about −3e+07.

choices.label: D
choices.rationale: This assumes the outputs settle at 0 near the asymptote, but the tangent function is undefined there and its values grow without bound in size.

title: evaluate arcsin, arccos or arctan of the matching trigonometric function at an angle outside the principal range, instea

choices.label: C
choices.rationale: This uses the reference angle with a positive sign; sin(7π/6) = −1/2, so the output must have a negative sine.

title: evaluate a trigonometric function of an inverse trigonometric value, using the principal range to fix the sign.
stem: What is the exact value of sin(arccos(−3/5))?

choices.label: A
choices.rationale: This gives sine a negative sign because the cosine is negative, but arccos returns an angle in [0, π], where sine is never negative.

choices.label: B
choices.rationale: This takes the magnitude of the given ratio, but the value asked for is the sine; the cosine is −3/5 and the sine is found from sin² = 1 − cos².

choices.label: C
choices.rationale: Correct: Let θ = arccos(−3/5), in [0, π]; cos θ = −3/5, so sin θ = √(1 − 9/25) = 4/5, positive in the second quadrant.

choices.rationale: This divides the sine 4/5 by the cosine magnitude 3/5, which gives a tangent-like ratio, not the sine.
